summary: Ephemeral approval token signed with rotated key is rejected by identity-proxy, blocking JIT bastion impersonation
description: Issue summary: Users are unable to open ephemeral bastion sessions created via the support runbook JIT flow. The approval appears to succeed in the Console, and Okta reports an approval token issuance, but the identity-proxy rejects the token and returns 403 which prevents the impersonation/SSH session from being established. Impact: Multiple oncall engineers and support staff cannot escalate into customer environments or run critical runbooks that require ephemeral bastion access. Business impact: operational friction for oncall, potential delay in incident remediations. Affected area: internal JIT access flow (Console -> Approval -> ephemeral token -> identity-proxy -> bastion).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to Console as a regular internal user (non-admin).
2) Start the support runbook that requests ephemeral bastion access (select target host in us-east).
3) Submit the JIT access request and approve it via the Console approval UI or approver email link.
4) From the Console click 'Open Bastion' or use the generated ephemeral token; identity-proxy responds with 403 and JSON: {"error":"invalid_token_signature"} and session is not established.
logs: 2026-03-13T18:02:17Z identity-proxy ERROR request_id=abcd1234 token_validation failed: signature verification failed (kid mismatch)
2026-03-13T18:02:18Z okta-audit INFO approval_issued user=a.patel approver=m.lee token_kid=legacy-key-2024 rotation_event=evt-2026-03-12
comments: Support (2026-03-13 18:05) - Aisha: Customer-facing runbooks blocked; users see 403 when trying to open bastion. Attached s3 logs and screenshots.

SRE (2026-03-13 18:20) - Marcus: Reproduced in prod/us-east. Identity-proxy returns token signature error. Initial hypothesis: key rotation mismatch between Okta-issued kid and identity-proxy keyset cache.

Auth (2026-03-13 19:10) - Priya: Confirmed an automated key rotation job ran 2026-03-12; Okta now issues tokens with kid=rotated-2026 but some services still verifying against archived keyset. Investigating keyset refresh timing.
Support (2026-03-14 08:25) - Aisha: Temporary mitigation accepted by SRE (adding legacy public key to identity-proxy trust store) allowed two engineers to proceed. Need permanent fix and postmortem.
Security (2026-03-14 09:00) - Elena: Add a follow-up to audit key rotation playbook and ensure automated keyset propagation has monitoring and alerting.
investigation_notes: Timeline: rotation job executed 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC. Okta started issuing tokens with new kid at 03:05 UTC. Some identity-proxy instances refreshed keys from JWKS at 03:07 UTC but a subset (autoscaled instances behind autoscaler) still had cached jwks from 02:50 and rejected rotated tokens. We reproduced by provisioning a new autoscaled identity-proxy pod with stale jwks cache and saw rejection. Hypothesis: jwks cache invalidation not propagated on pod bootstrap; autoscaler uses baked image with cached keys and does not fetch JWKS before accepting traffic. Alternative hypothesis: race between key rotation TTL and edge caching layer (cdn/nginx) causing forwarded tokens to hit older instances. We found a gap in startup initialization: identity-proxy expects JWKS cache to be present and does not proactively refresh on first request if file exists.
resolution: Mitigation (2026-03-14 08:30): temporarily added legacy public key into identity-proxy truststore and triggered rolling restart of all identity-proxy pods in prod/us-east; this accepted tokens again. Permanent fix: merged PR to identity-proxy to always fetch JWKS from Okta on startup and to add a background refresh with immediate invalidation after key-rotation webhook (PR linked below). Deployed canary 2026-03-14 11:00 and rollout completed 2026-03-14 12:15. Follow-ups: update Key Rotation Playbook, add monitoring alert for consecutive token signature failures > 5m, and add an e2e JIT access test that runs on key rotations.
next_steps: 1) QA to run JIT access smoke after next scheduled key rotation (owner: SRE).
2) Update deployment image build to not bake JWKS files; ensure first-run boot fetch (owner: infra).
3) Add Grafana alert for signature verification error spikes (owner: observability).
4) Run postmortem and share in #incidents and with Security for compliance evidence.
